# Disney+ Plans Compared: Every Plan, Bundle and Add-on Price, October 2026

Disney+ is $12.49 with ads, Premium $21.49 or $214.99 a year, the Hulu bundle $12.99 or $21.99, ESPN bundles to $44.99, NFL+ bundles $45.99 up. Every price on one page.

Published Oct 11, 2026 Checked against official sources · last verified Oct 11, 2026 · how we verify

Disney+ has two plans of its own and nine more that wrap it with Hulu, ESPN, HBO Max or NFL+. As of October 10, 2026, Disney+‘s plans and prices page lists Disney+ (With Ads) at $12.49 a month, Disney+ Premium at $21.49 a month or $214.99 a year, the Disney+, Hulu Bundle at $12.99 or $21.99, the ESPN bundles from $21.99 to $44.99, the HBO Max bundles at $21.99 or $34.99, and two NFL+ Premium bundles at $45.99 and $54.99. These are the prices for new subscriptions since September 23, 2026; the page says anyone who signed up earlier sees the change “in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.” This guide puts every price on one page, works out the arithmetic Disney’s page does not, and notes where the page is silent. If you are leaving, the billing paths are in our Disney+ cancellation guide.

## The quick answer

- Disney+ (With Ads): $12.49 a month, no annual option listed
- Disney+ Premium (No Ads): $21.49 a month, or $214.99 a year ($17.92 a month by our math)
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle: $12.99 with ads, $21.99 with no ads on both, 50 cents over Disney+ alone
- With ESPN: $21.99 or $32.99 with ESPN Select, $35.99 or $44.99 with ESPN Unlimited
- With HBO Max: $21.99 with ads, $34.99 with no ads, direct billing only
- With NFL+ Premium: $45.99 or $54.99, on the ESPN Unlimited bundles only
- Extra Member: $6.99 to $14.99 a month depending on plan
- Free trial: none. “Please note that Disney+ does not currently offer a free trial.”

# New Disney+ Pricing: What You'll Pay and How Much More

By WDWMAGIC Staff· Wednesday September 23, 2026 12:44pm ET·"Disney+"

 View 3 photos

WDWMAGIC+

 Disney+ prices have risen across most plans as of September 23, 2026. Premium tiers jumped 13.2%, while existing subscribers keep their current rate until October 21, 2026.

 Disney+ prices have risen across most plans as of September 23, 2026. Premium tiers jumped 13.2%, while existing subscribers keep their current rate until October 21, 2026. 

Photos / 3 in this gallery

 

Disney has raised prices on several Disney+ and bundle subscription plans. 

The Disney+ price increase applies to new subscriptions starting today, September 23, 2026. If you already have a Disney+ subscription, the new pricing will show up in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.

### New Disney+ Pricing and Percentage Increases

Here's what changed, including how much each plan went up by percentage:

- Disney+ (With Ads): $12.49, up from $11.99 — a 4.2% increase
- Disney+ Premium Monthly (No Ads): $21.49, up from $18.99 — a 13.2% increase
- Disney+ Premium Annual (No Ads): $214.99, up from $189.99 — a 13.2% increase
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium (No Ads): $21.99, up from $19.99 — a 10% increase
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Bundle (With Ads): $21.99, up from $19.99 — a 10% increase
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Bundle (No Ads): $34.99, up from $32.99 — a 6.1% increase

The Premium plans, both monthly and annual, saw the largest percentage jump at over 13%. The ad-supported Disney+ plan had the smallest increase, at just over 4%.

### When You'll See the Change

New subscribers pay the updated prices right away. If you're a current subscriber, your rate stays the same until your next billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026. Check your account settings for your exact renewal date so you know when the new price takes effect.

# Disney+ and Hulu Prices Rose in the U.S. — What Each Plan Costs Now

Disney+ and Hulu's U.S. ad-free plans now cost $21.49 a month. Compare September 2026 standalone and bundle prices, unchanged tiers, promotions and billing timing.

SA By Sara Avegaard Published September 24, 2026 at 7:08 PM CEST 3 min read

Official Hulu on Disney+ logo showing both streaming brands together. Disney+ Press

Disney+ and Hulu’s U.S. standalone plans now cost $12.49 a month with ads or $21.49 a month for Premium. The ad-free price is $2.50 higher than before; the ad-supported price is up 50 cents. The Disney+/Hulu bundle with ads remains $12.99 a month, while its Premium bundle rose to $21.99. New subscriber prices took effect September 23, 2026. Existing subscribers see the change on their next monthly bill, according to TheWrap’s price-change report.

These are standard U.S. monthly prices, before tax or any eligibility-limited offer. Disney currently advertises lower six-month introductory prices for some bundles; those offers renew at the regular rates shown below.

## What Changed in September 2026?

| U.S. plan | Previous monthly price | Current monthly price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+ with ads | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Disney+ Premium | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Hulu with ads | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Hulu Premium | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Disney+ + Hulu with ads | $12.99 | $12.99 | No change |
| Disney+ + Hulu Premium | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Select with ads | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Select Premium | $29.99 | $32.99 | +$3.00 |

The current rates come from Disney’s plan listings and Hulu. Previous rates and the timing of the increase come from contemporaneous reporting. Disney+ Premium also has a current $214.99 annual option; the table compares monthly plans only.

## Which Bundles Stayed the Same?

Disney’s current site still lists Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Unlimited at $35.99 a month with ads on Disney+ and Hulu, and $44.99 for the Premium Disney+/Hulu combination. Both Unlimited bundle prices were unchanged in the September price-change reporting. ESPN Select and Unlimited are different plans; do not compare their prices as if they contain the same sports access.

The Disney+/Hulu bundle with ads also stayed at $12.99. That is just 50 cents more than either ad-supported service alone at $12.49. The Premium duo at $21.99 is likewise 50 cents more than either $21.49 standalone Premium plan. That is a price comparison, not a claim that every viewer needs both services.

## What About HBO Max and Live TV?

Disney currently lists its Disney+ + Hulu + HBO Max bundle at $21.99 a month with ads or $34.99 without ads. Its Hulu + Live TV package, which includes Disney+ and ESPN Select, is $99.99 a month; the Premium Live TV combination is $109.99. Check the exact included services and any trial or promotion at checkout, because these are different packages from the two-service bundles above.

## When Will Existing Subscribers Pay More?

The September 23 rates applied to new U.S. sign-ups immediately. Existing monthly subscribers do not all get charged on the announcement date: the higher amount appears on their next billing cycle. Check your own account notice and renewal date for the precise charge. These prices do not describe Disney+ or Hulu subscriptions outside the U.S.

Disney’s current bundle page also offers eligible customers six months of the Disney+/Hulu ad-supported duo at $11.99 a month or the Premium duo at $19.99 a month, billed for the full six-month term. After that, they renew at $12.99 and $21.99 a month respectively. Those temporary prices are not the new standard rates.

For another recent streaming-price comparison, see what changed for Apple TV subscribers.

# Disney+ Price Hikes & Price History (2026)

Updated October 5, 2026 · Researched & fact-checked by Shaheer

Disney+ has raised the ad-free Premium plan four years running: $10.99 → $13.99 (2023) → $15.99 (2024) → $18.99 (October 2025) → $21.49 (September 23, 2026). The ad-supported tier climbed from $7.99 to $12.49 over the same period. The 2026 round was a 13% rise on Premium and 50 cents on the ad plan, and it took Disney+ past $20/month for the first time.

## At a glance

Current price

$21.49 (Premium (no Ads))

Last increase

September 23, 2026 (+13.2%)

Total change tracked

+95.5%

Tracked increases

5

## Key takeaways

- Disney+ has raised the ad-free Premium plan every year since 2023: $10.99 → $13.99 → $15.99 → $18.99 (October 2025).
- The ad-supported tier climbed from $7.99 to $11.99 over the same period.
- Disney deliberately widens the price gap to push subscribers toward the cheaper ad tier.
- The Disney+/Hulu/ESPN bundle is the main way to soften the per-service cost if you watch all three.
- Disney+ Premium is $21.49/month as of September 23, 2026 — past $20 for the first time, and the fourth increase in four years.
- The ad plan rose only 50 cents to $12.49 while ad-free rose $2.50, widening the gap to $9.00 a month.
- The ad-free Disney+/Hulu bundle at $21.99 now costs barely more than Disney+ Premium alone — 50 cents for a second service.
- Premium has risen 95% since 2023, from $10.99 to $21.49.

## Disney+ price increase history

| Date | Plan | Region | Old → New | Change | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| September 23, 2026 | Premium (no Ads) | US | $18.99 → $21.49 | +13.2% | Source |
| September 23, 2026 | Basic (with Ads) | US | $11.99 → $12.49 | +4.2% | Source |
| October 21, 2025 | Premium (no Ads) | US | $15.99 → $18.99 | +18.8% | Source |
| October 17, 2024 | Premium (no Ads) | US | $13.99 → $15.99 | +14.3% | Source |
| October 12, 2023 | Premium (no Ads) | US | $10.99 → $13.99 | +27.3% | Source |

## What Disney+ costs right now

- Basic (with Ads): $12.49 (US)
- Premium (no Ads): $21.49 (US)
- Premium (annual): $214.99 (US)
- Disney+/Hulu bundle (ad-free): $21.99 (US)
- Disney+/Hulu bundle (with Ads): $12.99 (US)

## Disney+ price history: $10.99 to $21.49 in four years

Disney+ has increased its ad-free Premium price three years running, from $10.99 in 2023 to $13.99, then $15.99, and $18.99 in October 2025. That is roughly a 73% rise in two years, one of the steepest in streaming.

The strategy is explicit: Disney widens the gap between the ad-free and ad-supported plans to nudge subscribers toward advertising, which it monetises separately. Leadership has framed ads as central to streaming profitability, so the ad-free tier absorbs most of the increases.

With Disney bundling Hulu and ESPN and changing plan structures frequently, it is easy to lose track of what you actually pay. Recording your real monthly charge is the only reliable way to catch each annual increase.

On reducing the cost, you have three realistic levers. The ad-supported tier at $11.99 is the cheapest way to keep watching. The annual Premium plan ($189.99) works out below twelve monthly payments if you stay subscribed year-round. And if you also watch Hulu or ESPN, the Disney bundle is priced below buying the services separately. Given Disney has raised the ad-free tier every year since 2023, treating another increase as likely and pre-deciding your ceiling is the sensible approach.

The September 23, 2026 round was the fourth in four years and the first to take Disney+ past $20: Premium went $18.99 to $21.49, a 13% rise, while the ad-supported plan moved just 50 cents to $12.49. Counting from 2023 the ad-free plan has gone $10.99 to $21.49 — 95%, close to a doubling in three years.

Disney+ and Hulu raise prices by up to 13 percent after doubling profits - Ars Technica

# Disney+ and Hulu raise prices by up to 13 percent after doubling profits 

 The Disney+ ad-free plan is now more expensive than Netflix’s. 

 Scharon Harding – Sep 23, 2026 5:18 pm | 126 

 

 A promotional image for the third season of The Mandalorian. Credit: Disney 

 A promotional image for the third season of The Mandalorian. Credit: Disney 

Disney+ got its fourth price hike in four years today. Hulu prices also went up.

Disney+ and Hulu’s respective standalone, ad-free plans (which also support 4K and HDR) are each increasing 13 percent from $19 per month to $21.50/month.

Disney+ and Hulu’s respective standalone plans with ads increased from $12 to $12.50.

The Walt Disney Company also increased prices for bundles of the streaming services, including those with ESPN.

The price for the Disney+ and Hulu bundle without ads increased from $20/month to $22/month. The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads ($13) didn’t get more expensive.

However, prices increased for the Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Select bundles with ads (from $20 to $22) and without ads (from $29 to $33).

Monthly subscription prices for Hulu + Live, which adds cable channels delivered over the Internet to Hulu’s on-demand options, went up by $10.

For comparison, Netflix is currently $9/month with ads and starts at $20/month without ads. There’s also a $27/month ad-free plan for premium features, like 4K. That means Disney+ and Hulu are both more expensive than the most popular streaming service now, unless you want 4K or HDR.

The last time that Disney+ raised prices was in October 2025. It also raised prices in October 2024, October 2023, and December 2022. It launched in 2019.

Hulu’s most recent price hikes occurred in October 2025, October 2024, October 2023, and October 2022. It launched in 2008.

Today’s price hikes follow Disney increasing the price for both tiers of its ESPN streaming service on September 17.

In its most recent quarterly earnings report, Disney reported that revenue from Disney+ and Hulu increased 11 percent. Operating income for Disney+ and Hulu combined increased 116 percent year over year to $712 million. Netflix, for comparison, reported operating income of $4.19 billion in its most recent earnings report. Netflix has many more subscribers (325 million as of January) than Disney+ (131.6 million as of September 2025) and Hulu (59.7 million subscribers for its on-demand streaming service as of September 2025).

Price hikes are likely part of Disney’s ongoing effort at streaming profitability. Netflix’s success shows there is still ample room for growth. The new prices may also steer customers more toward bundles, which streaming service providers believe lead to fewer cancellations and help Disney manage the unpredictable ads market.

 Scharon Harding Senior Technology Reporter

# Disney+ Price Increase Hits October 21: Why the $21.99 Hulu Bundle Beats $21.49 Premium, and How to Switch or Cancel First (2026)

 By Jordan Lee October 12, 2026 October 12, 2026 

Short answer: Existing Disney+ subscribers pay the new prices from their first bill on or after October 21, 2026. Premium goes from $18.99 to $21.49 a month. The plan with ads goes from $11.99 to $12.49. Here’s the odd part: the Disney+ and Hulu Premium bundle is $21.99, just 50 cents more than Disney+ Premium alone. The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads didn’t change at $12.99. If you pay for Premium by itself, the bundle or the ad tier is almost always the better deal now.

A $2.50 bump doesn’t sound like much. Over a year it’s $30, and Disney has now raised Disney+ prices roughly once a year since launch.

But the more interesting change isn’t the hike itself. Disney priced its plans so that Disney+ Premium on its own now looks like a bad deal next to the bundle. Once you see the numbers side by side, the “what should I do before October 21” question mostly answers itself.

Below is every new price, the plan math for the three most common situations, and how to switch or cancel cleanly before your renewal date.

## When does the Disney+ price increase hit existing subscribers?

Existing U.S. Disney+ subscribers are charged the new prices starting with their first billing date on or after October 21, 2026, while new subscribers have paid the higher rates since September 23, 2026, according to Disney’s announcement as reported by CBS News on September 23, 2026.

So the exact day depends on your billing date. If you’re billed on the 5th, your first higher charge lands November 5. If you’re billed on the 22nd, it lands October 22.

That’s useful. Most people have a week or more to decide.

## How much does each Disney+ plan cost now?

As of October 2026, Disney+ Premium costs $21.49 a month and Disney+ with ads costs $12.49 a month in the U.S., up from $18.99 and $11.99, while the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads stays at $12.99 a month, per Disney’s figures reported by CBS News and Variety.

## Is the Disney+ and Hulu bundle cheaper than Disney+ Premium alone?

The Disney+ and Hulu Premium bundle costs $21.99 a month after the October 2026 increase, only $0.50 more than Disney+ Premium alone at $21.49, so anyone paying for ad-free Disney+ by itself can add ad-free Hulu for 50 cents.

### What changed in 2026

Almost every service raised prices this year. Netflix increased all three plans in March, by $1 for its ad plan and $2 for both ad-free plans. Disney raised Disney+ and Hulu again in September, the fourth increase in four years, as we reported in Disney's 2026 price increase. YouTube Premium rose to $15.99, Peacock increased its plans in August and Amazon renamed its ad-free add-on Prime Video Ultra and raised it to $4.99.

Apple TV now costs $14.99 a month. Apple One, which bundles Apple TV with Apple Music and more, also rose, as our report on the Apple TV and Apple One price increase explains.

### Music streaming prices

Spotify Premium Individual costs $12.99 a month after a 2026 increase, with Duo at $18.99, Family at $21.99 and Student at $6.99. Apple Music costs $11.99 for individuals, $19.99 for families and $6.99 for students. Our comparison of Spotify and Apple Music looks beyond price.

### How much is everything?

Subscribing to Netflix Standard, the ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle, HBO Max Standard and Apple TV costs about $75 a month before tax. Add Spotify or Apple Music and YouTube Premium and it passes $100. That is why many households now rotate services rather than keeping them all.

### Six ways to pay less

Use bundles: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle costs only 50 cents more than one service. Try ad tiers if you mainly watch in the background. Rotate subscriptions around the shows you want. Check what your phone carrier, broadband plan or credit card includes. Pay annually where a service offers a discount. And review your subscriptions every few months. Ad-free Disney+ and Hulu now cost $21.49 a month each, but the ad-supported Disney+/Hulu Duo stays at $12.99. Here's every new price and when it hits your bill.

Hulu + Live TV Hits $99.99 as Disney Raises Disney+ and Hulu Prices Again featured image

Prices checked against hulu.com and disneyplus.com on Sep. 25, 2026. U.S. prices.

Hulu + Live TV now costs $99.99 a month in the U.S., up $10. Ad-free Disney+ and ad-free Hulu each jumped to $21.49 a month from $18.99, an increase of about 13%. The new prices took effect for new subscribers on Wednesday, Sep. 23, and already appear on Disney+ and Hulu's own sign-up pages.

One plan didn't move. The ad-supported Disney+/Hulu Duo Basic stays at $12.99 a month, only 50 cents more than Disney+ with Ads or Hulu with Ads on its own ($12.49 each). For most households, that makes it the best value in Disney's lineup.

It's Disney's fourth straight yearly price increase, after rounds in October 2023, October 2024 and October 2025. Disney didn't issue a press release. It updated its help center and confirmed the new prices to CBS News, which reported that the company "will continue pricing its most popular bundle, a joint Disney+/Hulu subscription with ads, at $12.99." The Wall Street Journal also reported the increase, citing a person familiar with the matter.

## The new Disney+, Hulu and bundle prices

## When existing subscribers pay more

New subscribers pay the new prices now. Disney's help center says existing subscribers will see the new price in billing cycles on or after Oct. 21, 2026. Variety, MacRumors and Cord Cutters News report that the higher price lands on current customers' next monthly bill. CBS News says it reaches existing subscribers "next month."

For Hulu + Live TV, StreamingBetter reports that existing subscribers will move to the new price on or after Oct. 21, 2026, depending on their billing cycle. Disney hasn't confirmed that date publicly. Last year's increase took effect on Oct. 21, 2025.

## What Hulu + Live TV includes

The $99.99 plan pairs the live TV lineup with Hulu with Ads, Disney+ with Ads and ESPN Select. The $109.99 Premium plan keeps the same ESPN tier but swaps in ad-free Hulu and Disney+ Premium. Hulu says both plans also include access to ESPN Unlimited content in the ESPN app, and ESPN's help center says the ESPN Unlimited entitlement is included with a Hulu + Live TV subscription. "No ads" applies only to on-demand shows. Live channels still carry commercials.

Both tiers include unlimited DVR at no extra cost, with recordings kept for up to nine months. Hulu offers a three-day free trial

Does Disney+ Have Ads on Every Plan? Premium and Live-Content Rules

# Does Disney+ Put Ads on All Plans? What to Know About Premium, Live Content, and Bundles

by GeekChamp Team 5 Oct 2026 2 min read

No. In the United States, Disney+ offers ad-supported and Premium plans. Premium on-demand movies and shows are generally free of commercial interruption, but select live and linear programming can include ads on any plan, and Premium may still include promotional or sponsored content. The exact plan names and prices depend on your country.

## How ads work on Disney+ plans

Disney+ distinguishes between on-demand movies and shows and select live or linear programming. On-demand content on Premium plans is generally free of commercial interruption; that qualification matters. Disney says that select live and linear programming can carry ads regardless of plan.

The Disney+ Help Center states: “Ads will be served in select live and linear programming, regardless of your Disney+ plan.” That policy means Premium is not a guarantee that every program or stream will be entirely free of advertising.

Disney’s Disney+ advertising policy describes these distinctions. “No Ads” in a plan name should therefore be read as a description of the plan’s on-demand viewing, not as a promise that no promotional material or live-programming ads will ever appear.

## US plan names and prices

As listed on Disney’s US plans page for new subscriptions as of September 23, 2026, the standalone options are Disney+ Basic/Standard (with Ads) at $11.99 per month and Disney+ Premium (No Ads) at $18.99 per month. The page also lists monthly and annual billing for Premium. These are US prices, not global rates; Disney warns that prices through third-party billing partners may vary.

Prices and available options can change. Check Disney’s US plans and prices page for the current offer before subscribing; the stated prices apply to new subscriptions and may not match third-party billing.

## A bundle can mix ad-supported and ad-free services

A bundle’s name or price does not tell you that every included service is ad-free. Check the Disney+ tier and the terms for each other service separately. Disney’s US listings include bundles with ad-supported Disney+ as well as Premium bundles where Disney+ on-demand viewing is generally free of commercial interruption. # Disney+ Premium Rises to $21.49/Month in Fourth Price Hike in Four Years

Disney+ Premium hits $21.49 a month on September 23, 2026, as the streamer raises ad-free prices for the fourth time since 2022

C. da Costa

Sep 23, 2026

Image: Disney+ Gadget Review

Key Takeaways

Key Takeaways

- Disney+ Premium rises 13% to $21.49/month, marking four price hikes in four years.
- Bundling ad-free Disney+ and Hulu saves subscribers roughly $21 per month over separate plans.
- Disney+ Premium remains $5.50 cheaper than Netflix Premium, though the gap keeps shrinking.

Disney+ has raised prices four times in four years. The latest increase takes effect September 23, 2026, pushing Disney+ Premium from $18.99 to $21.49 per month, a roughly 13% jump, according to Bloomberg and Variety. Existing monthly subscribers will see the new rate on their next billing cycle; annual plan and promotional pricing terms were not confirmed across all account types in available reporting. If you’re concerned about paying too much across your subscriptions, it may be worth a closer look at your monthly bills.

## What You’ll Pay Now

Here is the full breakdown of new U.S. monthly prices, per Bloomberg, Variety, and 9to5Mac.

| Plan | Old Price | New Price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+ Premium (ad-free) | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Hulu ad-free | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Disney+/Hulu ad-free bundle | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+ with ads | , | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Ad-supported Disney+/Hulu bundle | $12.99 | $12.99 | No change |

### The Bundle Math Still Works, Barely

Buying both ad-free plans separately now costs more than twice the bundle price.

Buying both standalone ad-free plans costs $42.98 per month, while the ad-free bundle comes in at $21.99, a savings of roughly $21 per month. The bundle is only $0.50 more than the price of either individual service alone, according to Bloomberg.

## Who Gets Hit and When

The new rates apply immediately to new subscribers, with existing monthly customers billed at the next cycle.

New subscribers pay the higher rate starting September 23, 2026. Existing monthly subscribers absorb the increase on their next billing cycle. Not all annual, grandfathered, and promotional pricing terms were clarified in available reporting.

### Disney+ vs. Netflix: The Gap Narrows

Disney+ Premium remains cheaper than Netflix Premium, though the margin between them continues to shrink.

At $21.49, Disney+ Premium still trails Netflix Premium’s reported $26.99 per month, according to Bloomberg. The $5.50 difference is real, though catalog depth and stream-limit policies vary between the two services.

### The Ad-Supported Tier at $12.49

For subscribers managing rising ad-free costs, Disney’s lower tier offers a clear alternative.

For subscribers managing multiple ad-free tiers, the ad-supported Disney+ plan at $12.49 per month is the most direct cost-reduction option Disney currently offers.
